transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... well, I guess I'm here because... I just feel like I can't really settle in my own body anymore. It's mostly when I'm supposed to just sit quietly and... deal with paperwork or, you know, shared household plans. So... yeah. That's mostly it.

{"intent": "Determine if the physical restlessness involves an uncomfortable urge specifically focused in the legs", "question": "When you feel like you can't settle, is that tied to an uncomfortable urge
Um... no. Not really. I don't think it's an urge like that.
Do you find yourself constantly worrying about a lot of different everyday things?
No, not really. I mean, I have things on my mind, like anyone else, but... I wouldn't say I'm constantly worrying about them.
Have you ever had periods where you felt fully rested and energized after only a few hours of sleep?
No. I sleep a normal amount. I've never really had anything like that happen.
Do you often have trouble keeping your focus on tasks or activities, such as work or conversations?

Yeah... I guess so. Um... if I sit down to read a planning email, or a chapter in a book, I usually start out fine. But... after a few minutes, I'll just be staring at the same paragraph. I'll realize none of it actually went in.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting, tapping your hands or feet, or squirming in your seat?

I guess... yeah. Um. Like, if we're at a family dinner, or... a church meeting. I'll usually be twisting my wedding ring, or... bouncing my foot. I try hard to look composed, but... I just end up shifting around in the chair a lot.
Did you experience similar difficulties with attention or restlessness when you were a child, before age 12?

I suppose... yeah. Looking back, it was already like that in elementary school. Um... I was always the one with a really messy desk. And I'd forget permission slips a lot. My teachers used to send notes home... just saying I talked out of turn, or... couldn't seem to stay in my seat. So... yes.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with persistent symptoms of both inattention (difficulty sustaining focus, reading without comprehension, disorganization, forgetfulness) and hyperactivity-impulsivity (fidgeting, foot tapping, squirming, inability to remain seated quietly, talking out of turn). A developmental history confirms that symptoms were present before age 12 in elementary school. Other conditions such as generalized anxiety disorder, bipolar disorder, and restless legs syndrome were screened and ruled out, consistent with a diagnosis of Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, combined presentation.
